H2	Background (Choose 1)
C	<b>SHERIFF</b> You keep order in Stonetop and protect it from outside threats. It might not be anything official, but everyone knows you've got a cool head and the weight to back up your words.
P	When you <b><i>bark an order or warning</i></b>, roll +CHA:
P	<b>on a 7+</b>, they must choose 1:
B	Do what you say
B	Dig in/take cover/flee
B	Attack you
P	<b>On a 10+</b>, you can sense which one they're about to do and act first if you like; gain advantage if you do.
C	<b>BLOOD-SOAKED PAST</b> You left behind a life of violence and a name mothers used to scare their children. For whatever reason, the people of Stonetop took you (back?) in and treat you like one of their own.
P	When you <b><i>Persuade using violence or threats against</i></b> <b><i>someone who knows your black reputation</i></b>, you can roll +STR instead of +CHA. Also, if you take the Formidable move, you can choose to roll +CON instead of +CHA.
P	When you <b><i>fight to kill without mercy or hesitation</i></b>, you deal +1d4 damage.
C	<b>STORM-MARKED</b> You've been touched by Tor (Rain-maker, Thunderhead, Slayer-of-Beasts!) and bear runic markings similar to those etched into the Stone. When did the marks manifest? Are they a symbol of your strength, speed, and courage? Or their source?
P	You start with the Storm Markings major arcanum.
P	Mark one of the boxes on the front of the Storm Markings sheet, and describe here the time you were struck by lightning and walked away unharmed:
H2	Instinct (Choose 1)
C	<b>PEACE</b> To avoid (further) bloodshed or violence.
C	<b>PRIDE</b> To maintain your dignity, to demand respect.
C	<b>RECKLESSNESS</b> To act without thought to the consequences.
C	<b>TROUBLE</b> To stick your nose in where it's unwelcome.
C	<b>VIOLENCE</b> To solve problems by force.

H2	Moves
P	You start with Dangerous, Hard to Kill, and either Armored OR Uncanny Reflexes.
HR
C	<b>ARMORED</b> When you <b><i>carry a shield</i></b>, mark only ◇ (instead of
P	• ◇◇ ). Also, you can ignore the <i>cumbersome</i> tag on any armor you wear.
P	If you take this move at the start of play, add an ◇◇ iron hauberk, ◇◇ bronze cuirass, or ◇◇ scale coat to your inventory (all are 2 armor,
P	<i>warm</i>, <i>cumbersome</i>).
C	<b>BATTLE JOY</b> When you <b><i>spill blood—yours or another's—and</i></b> <b><i>lose yourself in battle</i></b>, you ignore fear, pain, mindcontrol, and the effects of debilities as long as you keep fighting.
P	When <b><i>the action stops</i></b>, roll +CON: <b>on a 10+</b>, that was a rush, regain 1d4 HP; <b>on a 7-9</b>, you're winded and out of it, but you'll be fine with a few minutes' rest; <b>on a 6-</b>, mark a debility but don't mark XP.
C2	<b>BERSERKER</b>
P	(Requires Battle Joy)
P	While <b><i>in your Battle Joy</i></b>, add the <i>area</i> tag to your melee attacks, lashing out at anyone nearby (friend and foe alike). Roll damage separately for each target.
C	<b>CARVED OUT OF WOOD</b> Increase your max HP by 4.
CX	<b>DANGEROUS</b>
P	(Requires the Heavy)
P	When you <b><i>deal your damage</i></b>, you have advantage.
C	<b>FORMIDABLE</b> When you <b><i>wade into battle</i></b>, you can choose to roll +CHA: <b>on a 10+</b>, both; <b>on a 7-9</b>, pick 1:
B	Lesser foes will quail, hesitate, or flee before you.
B	Doughty foes will focus on you, seeing you as the greatest threat.
P	<b>On a 6-</b>, pick 1 but ask the GM what you've missed.
C	<b>FROSTY</b> When you <b><i>Defy Danger by keeping calm and carrying on</i></b>, <b>on a 10+</b> you can also ask the GM a question that you could ask when Seeking Insight. You have advantage on your next move to act on the answer.
HR
C	<b>GUARDIAN</b> When you <b><i>Defend</i></b>, hold 1 extra Readiness. Even on a 6-, hold 1 Readiness (plus whatever the GM says).
C	<b>IMPROVED STAT</b> Each time you take this move, increase one of your stats by 1 (to a max of +2).
HR
C	<b>INTIMIDATING</b> When you <b><i>Persuade using violence or threats</i></b>, you have advantage.
HR
CX	<b>HARD TO KILL</b>
P	When you <b><i>are at Death's Door,</i></b> you can roll +CON or +nothing (your choice). <b>On a 7-9</b>, you can mark a debility of your choice to regain 1 HP.
HR
C2	<b>UNSTOPPABLE</b> ◇◇◇◇◇
P	(Requires Hard to Kill)
P	When you <b><i>are reduced to 0 HP in battle</i></b>, you can keep fighting. Each time you take damage while at 0 HP, mark 1. If you would regain HP while fighting, clear one mark instead.
P	When you <b><i>stop fighting</i></b>, roll for Death's Door with a -1 penalty for each circle marked. If you survive, clear all your circles.
HR
C	<b>MUSCLEBOUND</b> (Requires Strength +2 or higher) When you <b><i>make a hand-to-hand or thrown attack</i></b>, it's <i>forceful</i> and <i>messy</i>. If it would already be <i>forceful</i> and/or <i>messy</i>, it's even more so.
PAGE	115
C	<b>PAYBACK</b> When you <b><i>deal damage to a foe that has harmed you</i></b> <b><i>or one of your allies</i></b>, deal +1d4 damage.
C	<b>RELENTLESS</b> When you <b><i>Clash and your foe survives</i></b>, you gain advantage the next time you Clash with them.
C	<b>SEASONED WARRIOR</b> (Requires level 2+ and the Heavy) Take a move from the Fox, Marshal, Ranger, or Seeker playbooks, for which you otherwise qualify. You can pick from a different playbook each time. (You can't pick Improved Stat or Superior Stat.)
C	<b>SITUATIONAL AWARENESS</b> When you <b><i>Seek Insight</i></b>, add the following to the list of questions you can ask:
Q	Who or what here is the biggest threat?
Q	What is my enemy's true position?
Q	What here can I use as a weapon?
P	When <b><i>a fight breaks out</i></b>, ask the GM 1 question that you could ask when Seeking Insight.
C	<b>UNCANNY REFLEXES</b> When you <b><i>are unarmored and carrying a normal or</i></b> <b><i>light load</i></b>, you impose disadvantage on any damage you take that you could dodge or roll with.
C	<b>UNFETTERED</b> When you <b><i>are subject to physical or mental restraint</i></b>, you may mark a debility to immediately break free of that restraint.
C	<b>TERROR ON THE FIELD</b> When you <b><i>reduce a foe to 0 HP</i></b>, describe how you take them out. If you fell them in a particularly brutal or impressive manner, their allies are impressed, dismayed, or frightened and respond accordingly.
C	<b>BRINGER OF RUIN</b> (Requires level 6+) When you <b><i>roll a 12+ to Clash and your foe survives</i></b>, name something they possess (like their sword, their position, a limb, their dignity, etc.), but nothing that would kill them outright. Whatever you name, it is broken, shattered, lost. Tell us how.
C	<b>CUT FROM GRANITE</b> (Requires level 6+ and Carved Out of Wood) Gain +1 armor (stacks with other sources) and increase your max HP by another 2 (+6 HP total).
C	<b>MIGHTY THEWS</b> (Requires level 6+ and Musclebound) When you <b><i>perform a feat of extraordinary strength</i></b> (bursting chains, smashing through a wall, heaving a boulder, etc.), you do it (OH YEAH!) but pick 1:
B	It takes a while
B	You cause unwanted damage or harm
B	It takes a toll (mark a debility)
C	<b>NEMESIS</b> (Requires level 6+ and Relentless) When you <b><i>Clash and your foe survives</i></b>, all of your future attacks against them do +1d6 damage.
C	<b>STEADFAST GUARDIAN</b> (Requires level 6+ and Guardian) While you <b><i>hold Readiness (from Defend)</i></b>, you can always suffer the damage/effects of an attack instead of your ward; no need to spend Readiness, you can just do it.
C	<b>STONE COLD</b> (Requires level 6+ and Frosty) When you <b><i>Defy Danger (or Struggle as One) by</i></b> <b><i>keeping calm and carrying on</i></b>, treat a 6- as a 7-9.
C	<b>SUPERIOR STAT</b> (Requires level 6+) Increase one of your stats by +1 (to a max of +3).

H2	A history of violence
P	Just about everyone here talks about the time you…
P	(pick 1 or 2)
C	… drove off a thunder drake that got too close to town.
C	… killed that hagr in the Foothills.
C	… slew a dozen crinwin in one battle.
C	… tossed those adventurers out of town.
C	… bested Ivan, the scariest bandit in Brennan's gang, the Claws.
C	… dragged yourself (and another?) into town, bleeding from a dozen wounds.
C	… were struck by lightning and woke up covered in these marks.
P	But folks are less keen to discuss… (pick 1 or 2)
C	… the look in your eye when you spilled all that blood.
C	… those hard cases who showed up looking for you.
C	… the shouting matches between you and your love.
C	… the time you spent as one of Brennan's Claws.
C	… what happened to Urbgen, even if he did have it coming.
C	… your uncontrollable seizures, where you claw those weird marks in the dirt.
P	What keeps you up at night? (pick 1 or 2)
C	That thrice-damned temper of yours.
C	The worry that someone's coming after you.
C	The feeling that the crinwin are getting bolder.
C	Wondering what Brennan's up to, now that he's the marshal of Marshedge.
C	Dark visions of things moving in the earth, restless, whispering, and hungry.
C	The question of who'll look after your family when you get yourself killed.
C	The worry that they'll all learn the truth about you, sooner or later.
H2	Introductions
P	Wait here for everyone else. When everyone's ready, take turns introducing your characters. When <b><i>someone reveals something and you want to know</i></b> <b><i>more</i></b>, ask them about it. When <b><i>someone asks you a</i></b> <b><i>question</i></b>, answer it truthfully.
STEP	1	On your first turn, <b>introduce yourself</b> by name, pronouns, background, origin, and appearance.
STEP	2	On your second turn, <b>describe your special</b> <b>possessions</b> and how you contribute to the village (beyond working the fields).
STEP	3	On your third turn, <b>tell us about your history</b> <b>of violence</b>, and what keeps you up at night.
STEP	4	On your next turn, <b>answer one of the following</b>, naming one or more NPCs who live in Stonetop.
C	Who is your closest kin?
C	Who is your lover/spouse/betrothed?
C	Who most needs/deserves your protection?
C	Whose forgiveness do you strive to earn?
STEP	5	Go around again. Answer another question from 4, or pass. When everyone has passed, go on.
STEP	6	On your next turn, <b>ask your fellow PCs one of</b> <b>these</b>. When others ask you, answer as you like.
C	Which one of you once dragged me home, bleeding and unconscious?
C	Which one of you can I trust to always have my back?
C	Which one of you has stayed my hand?
C	Which one of you has traded blows with me?
STEP	7	Go around again. Ask another question from 6, or pass. When everyone has passed, go on.
STEP	8	Add your home to the steading playbook. When everyone is done, let spring burst forth!
